title: Milk Came From Cold Wire, Yet Baby Monkeys Clung to Soft Cloth 17 Hours a Day
description:
Behavioral & Circuit Analysis — Harry Harlow (1958): Wire Milk Surrogate vs Soft Terrycloth Contact Comfort, grounded in Harry F. Harlow (1958) (American Psychologist). Empirical findings show that in 1958 at the University of Wisconsin, Harry Harlow tested eight newborn rhesus macaques raised with dual inanimate surrogates inside their home chambers.

Follow-up physiological and behavioral evidence demonstrates: One surrogate was built of bare welded wire mesh warmed by a radiant bulb; the second was an identical frame wrapped in cushioned sponge rubber and soft tan terrycloth.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Harry F. Harlow (1958). The nature of love. American Psychologist. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0047884
- Robert R. Sears (1982). Obituary: Harry Frederick Harlow (1905-1981). American Psychologist. https://doi.org/10.1037//0003-066x.37.11.1280
- William T. Mckinney (1996). Harry Harlow, 1905-1981. American Journal of Psychiatry. https://doi.org/10.1176/ajp.153.5.704
